comparator.name: Oudheidwetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: Joint VU/UvA ACASA Oudheidwetenschappen, RIO56704, Dutch track, full time. OER adopted VU26May/UvA9June2026. Ancient History is retained as the preselected neutral illustration among five Dutch specialisations, not an official default and not selected for UCR fit. OER11.1: Year1 compulsory48 plus two exploratory6-EC choices; post-propaedeutic common48, exactly one specialisation30, open30 and thesis12 including colloquium. Selected Seminar Ancient History and Classical Mythology are both permitted orientation choices. Eight common post-propaedeutic6-EC units include the Dutch Receptie en Creatief Schrijven. The five Ancient History specialisation units are each6EC. Thus 25components/180EC; no stacking alternative tracks or duplicate colloquium. Source PDF page23 visibly shows6EC for Classical Canon2 although extraction loses that cell. Post-propaedeutic examinations require a positive BSA; BSA48first-yearEC; thesis entry requires every Year1/2 course. Diagnostic Dutch test and remedial course are noncredit. Practical exercises Historical Sources, Objects in Context, Excursion and Reception have85percent attendance. Open30 permits at most12ECintroductory units, with specified minor/same-language exceptions up to24EC; outside VU/UvA courses require board permission; internship at most12EC within30. Eligible VU University minors need no prior consent; overlapping/closely corresponding compulsory units cannot be duplicated in Highlights of the Ancient World. Archaeology FieldSchool1 can replace reception only with board approval; not mandatory Ancient History fieldwork. Annual offerings can change.

routeSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 lists five specialisations under the Oudheidwetenschappen track (Oude Geschiedenis, Oude Nabije Oosten, Archeologie, Grieks, Latijn) and Article 11.1 requires exactly one 30-EC compulsory specialisation; none is formally the generic/default option. Ancient History and Archaeology are the least specialised of the five (neither presupposes acquisition of a specific ancient language, unlike Ancient Near Eastern Studies, Grieks and Latijn), so under the route-selection rule's least-specialised-general step they were treated as the two candidates remaining. Article 10.2's own listed order then places Oude Geschiedenis before Archeologie, and this official curriculum order was used as the neutral tie-break between them per the route-selection rule's final step. The selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered and does not depend on UCR fit.

exception.reason: UCR has genuine ancient-world study: global ancient craft/material culture, early-democratic Greek archaeology and Athenian democracy, classical and cross-cultural myth, ancient passages in philosophy, political thought, empire and warfare. These contributions remain sound. They do not establish the sustained ancient Mediterranean/Near-Eastern cultural-historical and textual/material source inquiry that defines this degree and its Ancient History specialisation. The proposed 24-course programme gives six heritage/art courses and five literature courses the appearance of ancient-world depth, although Renaissance Italy, modern museums, art historiography since the sixteenth century, general literary interpretation and modern film adaptation have different taught objects. Four rhetoric/communication courses are primarily skills, stylistics, contemporary persuasion and principally Dutch work with primary-school children; their classical origins do not turn all 30 EC into classical studies. The only advanced History Research Seminar actually investigates Walcheren in 1809, not an ancient topic. Greek Archaeology and Heritage and Ancient Democracy have substantial overlapping early-Greek democratic content, so counting both cannot supply missing Near-Eastern/Roman/social-historical breadth. Broad empires/warfare surveys preserve real ancient content, but do not supply the defining study of ancient evidence, religion, Roman change, ordinary ancient lives and a specialised ancient research progression. Replacing modern companions with other modern history, art, sociology or media courses changes the inquiry to general cultural heritage or humanities. Archaeology reconstruction still lacks a sustained archaeological theory/methods/cult/city/death sequence; language specialisations lack acquisition and original-language text progression; Near-Eastern reconstruction lacks Akkadian/cuneiform and Mesopotamian progression. A coherent 180-EC UCR humanities programme is therefore not enough to support a comparable alternative here. This judgment concerns the defining substance and progression, not a matching quota, title, isolated absent course, professional licence or the mere absence of an ancient language from the selected Ancient History route.

candidateAssessment.reason: Ancient craft/material culture and early Greek democracy are real; modern art/museum/history additions do not establish theory, cult, city, death/commemoration and field methods as a coherent archaeology progression.

candidateAssessment.label: Latin/Greek literary reconstruction

candidateAssessment.label: Ancient Near Eastern reconstruction

audience.programmeDescription: Ancient Studies at VU and the University of Amsterdam examines the ancient Mediterranean and Near East through texts, material remains, history, literature and philosophy. Students choose a specialisation and complete research on an ancient-world topic.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers genuine study of ancient material culture, Greek democracy, classical myth and aspects of ancient thought and history. Its wider literature, rhetoric, art and modern-history courses do not establish a complete programme centred on ancient-world evidence and specialist research. We show the verified external curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration includes two orientation choices, one 30 EC specialisation, 30 EC open study and a 12 EC thesis including colloquium. Ancient History is an illustration, not an official default. Post-first-year study requires a positive study recommendation; thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. Language testing, attendance, elective-level and approval conditions apply; future offerings can change.
